title: Recover the AtlasOps service-health dashboard

bridge.knownConcept: Redundancy, stale state, and service degradation
bridge.applicationConcept: Provider adapters, caches, revalidation, loading states, and graceful degradation
bridge.analogyLimit: Cached application data can remain intentionally usable while stale; it is not equivalent to an active redundant network path.

buildBrief: Build a typed AtlasOps dashboard showing service status, last verified time, provider source, loading, empty, error, and stale states through one adapter boundary.
incidentBrief: The upstream provider becomes unavailable while an expired cache exists. Prevent false green status, show data age, serve the safe fallback, and bound retries.

scenario.symptoms: The dashboard initially labels expired cached data as current after the provider fails.

acceptanceTests: The UI distinguishes current, stale, unavailable, empty, and loading states without relying on color
Provider-specific payloads do not reach presentation components
Retry and cache tests prove bounded behavior and visible freshness
predictionQuestions: What should the user see when stale data is safer than no data?
Where should provider-specific fields stop propagating?
defenseQuestions: Trace a refresh through route, adapter, cache, and UI.
Explain why stale must not be displayed as healthy current data.
Change the freshness threshold and update its test.
hints: Treat data value and data freshness as different fields.
Put provider translation and retry policy behind one server adapter.
Use a finite retry budget and an explicit last-verified timestamp.
